title: Mesoamerican proportional design and astronomical dualities: rational approximations consistent with $φ$ and $π$ in calendrics and architecture
summary: Understanding how ancient Mesoamerican societies integrated mathematical ideas into calendrical design and monumental architecture requires approaches that acknowledge their distinct epistemological frameworks. While explicit textual evidence for concepts such as $π$ or the golden ratio $φ$ is absent, numerical patterns embedded in Mesoamerican calendars, iconography, and ritual architecture reveal a coherent system of proportional reasoning grounded in simple integer ratios.
